extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and evaluating a constitutional Charter of Rights and related political measures (assembly procedure, legislative/fiscal authority, individual liberty protections, military subordination, press liability, debt assumption), plus practical policy guidance on navigation, infrastructure, and debt negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual assembly and self-regulation of States General
rubrics_metrics.description: The States General shall assemble, uncalled, on the first day of November, annually, and shall remain together so long as they shall see cause. They shall regulate their own elections and proceedings, and until they shall ordain otherwise, their elections shall be in the forms observed in the present year, and shall be triennial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets mandatory meeting schedule, grants the body authority to regulate its own electoral and procedural rules, and fixes an interim electoral cadence (triennial) until changed by the body itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive fiscal authority of the States General
rubrics_metrics.description: The States General alone shall levy money on the nation, and shall appropriate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts sole legislative control over taxation and appropriation; places fiscal initiation and allocation exclusively with the representative assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative enactment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws shall be made by the States General only, with the consent of the King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines lawmaking as the province of the States General with a required concurrence from the sovereign; frames legislative-executive interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of personal liberty and judicial remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be restrained of his liberty, but by regular process from a court of justice, authorized by a general law. (Except that a Noble may be imprisoned by order of a court of justice, on the prayer of twelve of his nearest relations.) On complaint of an unlawful imprisonment, to any judge whatever, he shall have the prisoner immediately brought before him, and shall discharge him, if his imprisonment be unlawful. The officer, in whose custody the prisoner is, shall obey the orders of the judge; and both judge and officer shall be responsible, civilly and criminally, for a failure of duty herein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes due process as the sole lawful basis for detention, provides an immediate judicial remedy for unlawful imprisonment, mandates obedience by custodial officers to judicial orders, and imposes civil and criminal liability for failures — includes a stated (limited) exception for nobles via a specified private petition procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian supremacy over the military
rubrics_metrics.description: The military shall be subordinate to the civil authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms principle of military subordination to civilian institutions and legal authority; intended as a constitutional check on military power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press liability without broader restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Printers shall be liable to legal prosecution for printing and publishing false facts, injurious to the party prosecuting; but they shall be under no other restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits post-publication legal accountability for defamatory or false factual publications while rejecting other (e.g., prior) restraints on printing; balances freedom of the press with remedies for injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolition of pecuniary privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: All pecuniary privileges and exemptions, enjoyed by any description of persons, are abolished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes tax/exemption-based privileged financial statuses to promote fiscal equality among subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption and pledge for royal debts
rubrics_metrics.description: All debts already contracted by the King, are hereby made the debts of the nation; and the faith thereof is pledged for their payment in due time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a constitutional guarantee that prior sovereign obligations become national obligations, with the nation's faith pledged to satisfy them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary fiscal grant and tax continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Eighty millions of livres are now granted to the King, to be raised by loan, and reimbursed by the nation: and the taxes heretofore paid, shall continue to be paid to the end of the present year, and no longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines a one-time loan-granting measure with a temporal limit on existing taxes to manage immediate fiscal needs while signaling an end-date for prior tax regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal separation and reconvening schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The States General shall now separate, and meet again on the 1st day of November next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes formal adjournment and a fixed date for reconvening; implements the calendar element of constitutional procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal ratification/signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Signed by the King, and by every member individually, and in his presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires individual and in-person signatures of the sovereign and each member as a mode of validating the Charter; a formal ratification safeguard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and constitution of the assembly via common chamber
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commons inviting the two other orders to come and take their places in the common chamber; the chamber thus composed will declare that the States General are constituted, will notify it to the King, and that they are ready to proceed to business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for constituting a national assembly by forming a common chamber of orders, verifying powers, notifying the sovereign, and beginning legislative work; provides a constitutional path when orders disagree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactical use of taxation to secure assembly's continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppress all taxes, and instantly re-establish them till the end of their session, in order to prevent a premature dissolution: and then they will go to work on a declaration of rights and a constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy/tactical recommendation: suspending and immediately reconstituting tax authority to avoid executive forced dissolution while asserting assembly's control over fiscal and constitutional agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigability standard for inland waterways
rubrics_metrics.description: It is reduced to a maxim, that whenever there is water enough to float a batteau, there may be navigation for a batteau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes a practical threshold for considering waterways navigable (sufficient depth for small craft), implying engineering interventions (canals/locks) can extend navigability; used to justify investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public funding and interstate cooperation for major navigation works
rubrics_metrics.description: The States of Maryland and Virginia should make a common object of it. The navigation, again, between Elizabeth River and the Sound is of vast importance, and in my opinion, it is much better that these should be done at public than private expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates that major inter-jurisdictional navigation/infrastructure projects be pursued jointly by the relevant states and funded publicly rather than left to private interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precondition of indigenous negotiation/settlement before canal execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Probably, negotiation with the Indians, perhaps even settlement, must precede the execution of the Cayahoga canal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats negotiation/arrangement with indigenous peoples as a prerequisite for infrastructure development on or through their lands; acknowledges political and ethical necessity before construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction and contractual preservation in debt settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The debts due before the war ought to be distinguished from the debts contracted since, and all and every mode of payment and remittance under which they might have been discharged at the time they were contracted, ought to accompany those debts so long as any of them shall continue unpaid, because the circumstances of payment became united with the debt, and cannot be separated by subsequent acts of one side only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for treating pre-war and post-war debts differently in negotiations and for preserving the original contractual/payment mechanisms attached to debts as inseparable to avoid retroactive unilateral alteration; presents this as a negotiation lever in international debt settlement.
